U.S. and China agree to launch a formal AI dialogue, including a proposed channel for notifying each other about national-security incidents involving AI.

The move comes as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Vice Premier He Lifeng held New York talks on September 20 ahead of Xi Jinping’s scheduled September 23–25 U.S. state visit and meeting with President Trump.

Negotiations also cover tariffs, agricultural purchases, investment and rare earths; a Bloomberg-cited report said the sides discussed easing barriers on $30 billion of goods from each country.

What to watch: the tariff truce remains temporary, China’s agricultural commitments remain outstanding, rare-earth tensions persist, and chip export controls were not on the reported agenda.

items.text:
My first startup was hijacked by men with better resources.

This was before AI could code much more than a fucking template.

Anyone in San Francisco with money and connections could hire developers. He was in San Francisco.

Me? I built the support base myself.

I built around 300 Facebook groups and ran most of them myself. Around 500,000 members total across the U.S. and U.K.

While my app was still being built, another app started using trademark and search tactics that funneled people toward his product.

I did everything right and still couldn’t understand why, on release day, so many people kept asking me:

“Which app is yours?”

Then I saw it.

His app was at the top of the results no matter how people searched for what I had spent all that time building a community around.

So I went down the rabbit hole.

Within about five months, he had serious money behind him.

Jeffrey Katzenberg.
DreamWorks co-founder and former CEO of DreamWorks Animation.

Sujay Jaswa.
Former CFO of Dropbox and venture investor.

Yep.

I built an app. I built the community. I helped create a whole new niche in the App Store that became interesting enough to attract people operating at that level.

It just wasn’t my work they funded.

They hit 10M downloads and $2M MRR

10 million downloads and $2M MRR.

That’s $24M ARR.

Two years later, I’m living VA check to VA check. I bootstrap everything because I refuse to stop building, and as of today I have $0 in my account until the 1st.

That part burns.

Not because somebody else made money.

Because I know my shit is good.

I know I can build. I know I can see markets before they’re obvious. I know what I’m capable of because I’ve already watched something I helped see early turn into a market worth millions a year.

But being right and being able to capitalize on being right are two very different things.

Resources matter. Distribution matters. Timing matters. Capital matters.

And sometimes the person with the idea is broke while the machine built around the opportunity prints millions.

yeah, it fucking burns.

But I’m still building.

$0 in the account didn’t make me stop.

It just means I’m still in the part of the story nobody gives a shit about until after it works.

Yep. I knew those numbers would hit too. They hit all my predictions

And there’s another part of this story people don’t know.

I didn’t spend my 20s and 30s climbing the tech ladder.

I lost a lot of those years dealing with what I brought home from combat. I had to learn how to live life around it first.

I was 39 when I did this.

I’m fucking tired of salesmen taking builders’ shit.

I’m tired of watching people with better resources and better distribution step in front of the people who actually created something.

And now AI has made that easier than ever.

You can imitate the output.
You can copy the language.
You can package somebody else’s idea better than they can.
You can outsell the person who actually understands the thing.

But you cannot fake what’s underneath the hood forever.

Some of us paid a hell of a price to get here.

I want you none technical salesmen to read this shit.

items.text:
Vibe coding is changing how apps are built in 2026

A few years ago building a mobile app could take months and require a full development team.

Now AI can help you go from an idea to a working MVP much faster by generating UI screens, backend logic, APIs and even database setup from simple prompts.

And this is not limited to one type of app.

Food delivery, ecommerce, appointment booking, real estate, learning platforms, fitness apps, taxi apps, social communities, healthcare apps and SaaS dashboards can all be built much faster with these AI powered workflows.

But the interesting part is the platforms behind this shift.

1. Emergent

-> Emergent focuses on full stack AI development and can generate React Native apps along with backend automation, database setup and deployment workflows.

It can be useful for startups, SaaS products, marketplaces and custom business applications.

2. FlutterFlow

-> FlutterFlow combines a visual builder with AI assistance and uses Flutter for cross platform mobile development.

It is useful when you want polished mobile interfaces, Firebase integration and Android and iOS support.

3. Rork

-> Rork focuses on generating React Native mobile apps from prompts and is built around quick prototyping and idea validation.

This makes it useful for founders and teams that want to test an idea quickly before investing heavily in development.

But here is the part people often miss.

Vibe coding does not mean traditional development is dead.

AI works extremely well for MVPs, SaaS products, admin dashboards, business apps and marketplace products.

But complex enterprise systems, advanced AI integrations, performance optimization, security architecture and high scale infrastructure still need experienced developers.

The real advantage is not replacing developers.

It is giving developers much more leverage.

You can move faster, reduce repetitive engineering work, test MVP ideas earlier and make changes faster based on real user feedback.

But you still need proper planning, UI and UX decisions, architecture, custom integrations, security, deployment, maintenance and scaling.

Even if AI builds the first version of your app, the product still needs to be maintained, monitored and improved after launch.

And choosing the right platform also depends on what you are actually building.

Emergent is focused more on full stack applications.

FlutterFlow is strong for visual mobile development and polished UI.

Rork is focused more on fast React Native prototyping and idea validation.

So the biggest lesson for me is simple.

AI has made building apps much easier.

But building the app is only one part of creating a successful product.

You still need to know what to build, who you are building for, how the system should work and how you will scale it when people start using it.

Vibe coding makes development faster.

Good product thinking makes the development worth doing.
